name: FTMO
desc: The industry benchmark since 2015. 4.5M+ customers, $650M+ paid in rewards, 4.8 Trustpilot.
tags: Completed acquisition of regulated broker OANDA from CVC, Dec 2025
review: FTMO remains the reference point the rest of the industry is measured against. The numbers that matter: a 90% split from day one on the 1-Step, a fully refunded fee on the 2-Step, and a decade-long payout record - $650M+ paid since 2015. The trade-off is discipline: the 1-Step carries an EOD-trailing drawdown and a best-day rule, and Standard accounts face news and weekend restrictions once funded (choose the Swing account type to remove both). In December 2025, FTMO completed its acquisition of OANDA — one of the oldest regulated forex brokers globally — from CVC Capital Partners, making FTMO the parent of a licensed brokerage rather than just a challenge provider. Pricing is mid-market, but you are paying for the firm least likely to change the rules under you.

trustNote: Tens of thousands of reviews (exact count not confirmed).
name: FundedNext
desc: Multiple challenge models plus a rare perk: you earn 15% of profits made during the challenge itself.
review: FundedNext, launched in 2022 out of Dubai, differentiates itself with a genuinely unusual perk: 15% of the profits made during the challenge phase itself is paid out once you're funded - most firms pay nothing until the evaluation is cleared. The Stellar 1-Step keeps a 6% EOD-trailing drawdown and news-trading restrictions, while the Stellar 2-Step swaps to a static 10% drawdown with no news or weekend restrictions, giving traders a real choice between speed and flexibility. A 95% split is available as a paid add-on on top of the 80% base, and the newer Flex Challenge (May 2026) drops its consistency rule once funded. Pricing starts around $59 for a $6K account, scaling to just under $1,100 for $200K. FundedNext also runs a futures offering alongside forex, and carries a 4.5/5 rating on Trustpilot from tens of thousands of reviews - one of the stronger reputations in the mid-market tier.

name: The5ers
desc: Established 2016, 262K funded traders, scaling to $4M. Known for reliable payouts and no hidden rules.
review: The5ers has built its reputation on paying out without drama - 262K funded traders and a 10-year record back that up. The program menu is broad: instant funding (Hyper Growth), the flagship High-Stakes 2-step, and a Bootcamp route where most of the fee is only due after you pass. Static drawdowns across programs make risk math simpler than trailing-drawdown competitors. Splits start lower than rivals (50-75% on some routes) but scale with account growth, and the $4M scaling ceiling is among the highest anywhere.

name: Funding Pips
desc: Aggressively priced challenges with payout-cycle-based splits reaching 100% on the monthly cycle.
tags: Weekend holds paused on funded (temp, since Jan 2026)
review: Funding Pips built its reputation on aggressive pricing - 2-Step challenges start around $36 for a $5K account - paired with a split structure that rewards patience: choose the monthly payout cycle and keep 100% of profits, or take 60% weekly if you want cash faster. The 1-Step Master account can also reach 100% on its monthly cycle, though the 90%-on-demand option carries a 35% consistency rule. The instant Zero account skips evaluation entirely for a fixed 95% split, but enforces a hard rule against holding positions into the weekend - stricter than the firm's evaluated accounts, which only restrict weekend holding on funded accounts as of a January 2026 rule change. Founded in Dubai in late 2022, Funding Pips has since paid out more than $200 million, verifiable on the Rise blockchain, and holds a 4.5/5 Trustpilot rating from over 62,000 reviews - among the highest review volumes in the industry.

name: E8 Markets
desc: Build-your-own challenge: choose your drawdown, daily loss limit, and profit split at checkout.
review: E8 Markets' defining feature is checkout-level customization: on the E8 One challenge, traders pick their own drawdown (4-14%), daily loss limit (3-9.2%) and profit split (80-100%) before paying, with price scaling to match the risk profile chosen - a $5K account starts at $40, a $500K account runs into the thousands. That flexibility is unusual in a market where most firms fix the rules and let you pick only the account size. The newer E8 Zero, launched July 2026, trades that customization for simplicity: a flat 3% static drawdown and 80% split, aimed at traders who'd rather not build their own rule set. E8 also offers the largest account sizes tracked here, up to $500K. Formerly E8 Funding, the firm was founded in November 2021 and carries a 4.4/5 Trustpilot rating from over 3,200 reviews - solid, if with a smaller review base than some larger rivals.

trustNote: Lowest score among the well-established futures firms tracked, but no fake-review or suspension flags — complaints center on strict rule enforcement during drawdown events.
name: Topstep
desc: The longest-running futures funding firm — $1.5B+ paid out, 99.26% payout approval, and a single 'One Rule' max-loss limit with no separate daily loss cap.
tags: One Rule — single max-loss limit, no separate daily loss cap
$149 activation fee + monthly reset fee on failed Combines
Payout caps per request (up to $12,000, tiered by size)
2026 federal lawsuit alleges deceptive Live Program rule changes and cut payout caps ~50-60% in April 2026 — not addressed on Topstep's own site; unconfirmed beyond trader/legal reporting
Data breach disclosed Aug 4, 2026 — names, SSNs, DOB and medical info reportedly exposed; reported to IL/TX Attorneys General
review: Topstep is the original futures prop firm — 15+ years in, $1.5B+ paid out, and a 99.26% payout approval rate it advertises prominently. The Trading Combine is subscription-based ($49-$199/month by size) with a flat 90/10 split on qualifying payouts and a single 'One Rule' max-loss limit that replaced the old daily-loss-plus-trailing-drawdown structure — simpler to track, though it also means there's no separate daily circuit breaker. An optional 'Responsible Trading Advantage' toggle doubles your payout caps for a small monthly add-on. Getting funded requires hitting the profit target without breaching the One Rule and clearing a 50% consistency target; payouts are capped at 50% of account balance per request, up to $12,000 on the $150K tier. Reset fees and a $149 Express Funded activation fee apply on top of the subscription. Worth knowing before signing up: a federal lawsuit filed in 2026 accuses Topstep of retroactively tightening rules on its Live Program and trapping earned capital behind near-impossible reserve requirements, and trader communities reported payout caps were cut roughly 50-60% in April 2026. Topstep hasn't addressed either publicly on its own site as of this writing — worth independently checking court records and recent trader reports before committing capital. Separately, Topstep disclosed a data breach to the Illinois and Texas Attorneys General on August 4, 2026, reportedly involving names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth and medical information — worth watching for a customer notification and considering a credit freeze if you're an affected user.

trustNote: Reported as 'mid-4s' across tens of thousands of reviews — precise current figure not confirmed.
name: Apex Trader Funding
desc: High-volume favorite. One-time evaluation fees since the 4.0 update, with 100% of your first $25K profit.
review: Apex Trader Funding is one of the highest-volume names in futures prop trading, built around a simple pitch: pass a one-time-fee evaluation (no monthly subscription) and keep 100% of your first $25K in profit before settling into a 90/10 split. Two evaluation tracks are offered - EOD trailing drawdown or intraday trailing, which follows open equity in real time rather than just closed trades - both with no daily loss limit, unusual for the category. List prices are almost never what traders actually pay: 70-90% discount codes are in near-constant circulation, and a $25K EOD evaluation lists at $137 before those codes. A $99 (EOD) or $79 (intraday) activation fee applies once funded, and payouts run on 5-day cycles gated by a 50% consistency rule. Founded in 2021, Apex has stated it has paid out more than $800 million to traders and holds a Trustpilot rating in the mid-4s from tens of thousands of reviews - a track record few futures firms can match at this scale.

name: MyFundedFutures
desc: Modern plan lineup (Core, Rapid, Pro) with no activation fees and payout terms tuned per plan.
review: MyFundedFutures is one of the newer futures firms here, launched in November 2023, but it's already built an unusually strong reputation - a 4.9/5 Trustpilot rating from more than 18,000 reviews, among the highest of any firm tracked. The three-plan lineup (Core, Rapid, Pro) skips activation fees entirely, a real cost saving versus firms that charge $99-$149 once you're funded. Rapid stands out for dropping the consistency rule altogether, though its drawdown floor tracks real-time equity including unrealized P&L rather than just closed trades - worth understanding before you trade it. Core keeps a more traditional EOD drawdown with a 40% consistency requirement and a $5,000 cap per payout cycle, while Pro raises the cumulative payout cap to $100,000 with a $1,000 minimum per request. All three start at a $50K account (Core from $65/mo); pricing above $50K is estimated rather than confirmed. For traders who want a newer firm with a fast-growing review base, this is a strong candidate.

name: TradeDay
desc: Trader-friendly single-phase evaluation with no daily loss limit and splits that scale to 95%.
review: TradeDay keeps its evaluation deliberately simple: one phase, no time limit, and no daily loss limit at all - a rarity among futures prop firms, most of which enforce a hard daily stop. The trade-off is a 30% consistency rule and a trailing max drawdown that follows your account's high-water mark. Payouts are on-demand once you qualify rather than fixed to a calendar, and the split scales through three tiers - 80%, 90%, then 95% - as you build a track record, among the highest ceilings in futures funding. A $50K evaluation starts at $62.50/mo, with $100K and $150K accounts priced proportionally higher. Founded in Chicago in 2020 by James Thorpe and Steve Miley, TradeDay has a smaller but strong review base - a 4.6/5 Trustpilot rating from over 1,300 reviews - putting it toward the top of the pack on reputation, if with less volume behind it than the largest firms.

name: Alpha Capital Group
desc: UK-based firm with four evaluation paths (Alpha One, Pro, Swing, 3-Step) and zero listed commissions.
review: Alpha Capital Group runs four separate evaluation paths - Alpha One, Pro, Swing and a 3-Step - giving traders more route options than most UK-based firms offer, all with zero listed commissions. The Pro 2-Step entry starts at $50 for a $5K account: 80% split, 10% static drawdown, 5% daily loss, and a bi-weekly payout cycle. News trading is restricted once funded, in line with most forex challenge providers. Founded in London in November 2021 by George Kohler, Alpha Capital has scaled quickly and reports having paid out more than $62 million to traders. Its 4.7-star Trustpilot rating from over 21,000 reviews is among the highest of any firm in this comparison - though, as with most large prop firms, a subset of negative reviews cite payout denials and account closures tied to rule violations. Read the specific complaint pattern before committing beyond the entry tier, and keep meticulous records of every trade.

trustNote: Trustpilot rating is inconsistent across sources and the listing has been flagged for guideline issues at times — treat any single aggregate score with caution.
name: Goat Funded Trader
desc: Among the cheapest challenges in the industry, with an unusually broad instrument list (stocks, ETFs, crypto).
review: Goat Funded Trader competes almost entirely on price and breadth: a Classic 2-Step challenge on a $5K account lists at just $22, among the cheapest entries in the industry, and the instrument list runs to more than 14,000 symbols including stocks, ETFs and crypto alongside forex - far broader than most challenge providers. Rules on the Classic 2-Step are otherwise standard for the category: 10% static drawdown, 5% daily loss, and news, EA and weekend trading all permitted. Splits start at 80% and can reach 100% via paid add-ons, and scaling runs up to $800K. Goat launched in 2022-2023 (sources differ on the exact date) and is still building a durable trust record - its Trustpilot rating is mixed and inconsistent across sources, with the platform flagged for guideline issues at times, so it's worth reading recent, dated reviews rather than relying on the aggregate score before committing beyond the cheapest entry tier.

name: Maven Trading
desc: Budget-friendly firm with five challenge types from $15 and bi-weekly payouts.
review: Maven Trading competes on accessibility: five challenge types spanning Mini, 1/2/3-Step and Instant, with the cheapest entry in our entire dataset - a 3-Step Mini on a $2K account for $15. That's a genuine low-stakes way to test a strategy before committing real money elsewhere. The Instant Funding option skips evaluation entirely but trades convenience for tighter risk limits: a $100K instant account runs a 3% trailing drawdown, 2% daily loss and a 20% consistency rule, considerably stricter than Maven's staged challenges. Splits are a flat 80% across the lineup, with payouts on a roughly bi-weekly cycle. Founded in 2022, Maven has built a strong reputation fast - a 4.6-star Trustpilot rating from more than 5,000 reviews, with roughly 85% five-star, and the firm reports over $60 million funded to more than 5,000 traders. For traders who want to test Maven cheaply before scaling up, the $15 Mini entry is close to unique in the market.

name: FTUK
desc: Instant funding and evaluations with scaling up to $6.4M and weekly payouts.
review: FTUK pairs evaluations with genuine instant funding, and its standout number is scale — accounts can grow to $6.4M, among the highest ceilings tracked here, with a flat 80% split throughout. The Flex Challenge only charges once you pass (a $50K account currently runs $235 on a promo code against a $509 list price), which shifts the financial risk of failing an evaluation away from the trader, a rarer structure in the CFD-challenge space. FTUK claims a weekly payout cycle, faster than the bi-weekly norm at most rivals, though that cadence isn't independently confirmed. Trustpilot ratings vary by source — from roughly 3.9 to 4.4 out of 5 — with recurring complaints about account violations and payout delays alongside positive reports. Sources also disagree on FTUK's founding: some place it as far back as February 2021, longer than the four years currently tracked here. Pricing and rules haven't been independently verified on FTUK's own site yet, so confirm current terms before funding.

name: City Traders Imperium
desc: Instant funding with a 6% static drawdown, splits scaling 70→100%, and a $500 monthly salary feature.
review: City Traders Imperium's headline feature is a $500/month "salary" paid to funded traders independent of trading profit — a rare structure among evaluation-based firms. Splits start around 70% and scale to 100% with performance, and the 2-Step Challenge is priced aggressively: $29 for a $2.5K account, with the fee reportedly refundable on a pass. An Instant option skips evaluation entirely (an $80K account currently runs $1,359 on a promo against a $1,599 list price), both tracks running a 6% static drawdown. CTI carries a solid 4.3/5 Trustpilot rating from nearly 1,700 reviews. One flag worth noting: our data tracks CTI at 3 years old, but multiple review sites place its founding as far back as 2018 under founder Daniel Martin — a discrepancy of several years worth confirming directly before treating either figure as settled. Pricing beyond the entries above hasn't been independently verified on citytradersimperium.com yet.

trustNote: Trustpilot rating display was suspended after Trustpilot removed fake reviews from this listing (last visible score ~3.6 from 2,000+ reviews before removal).
name: Blue Guardian
desc: Four funding plans with a 24-hour payout guarantee and $20M+ in verified payouts.
review: Blue Guardian's pitch centers on speed — a 24-hour payout guarantee and more than $20M in verified payouts to date — across four funding tracks scaling up to $4M, with splits reaching 90%. It added a futures evaluation track in 2026 alongside its original offering; the plans currently tracked here (a $25K evaluation at $48, $50K at $119, and a $995 $150K Instant account with a 6% overall / 3% daily drawdown) are all from that newer futures side. The one point that needs real caution: Trustpilot suspended Blue Guardian's public rating display after removing a batch of fake reviews from its listing, leaving a last-visible score of roughly 3.6 from over 2,000 reviews that can no longer be treated as a clean signal. Review content that remains shows a real split — mostly positive, but a meaningful one-star cluster citing account closures and payout denials. Read recent, dated reviews rather than any aggregate score, and confirm terms directly before funding.

name: ThinkCapital
desc: Backed by broker ThinkMarkets (FCA/ASIC-regulated). Bolt instant program with bi-weekly payouts.
review: ThinkCapital runs on the infrastructure of ThinkMarkets, an FCA/ASIC-regulated broker, which lends it more institutional backing than most independent challenge providers. Its Bolt instant-funding track pays out every 14 days, and splits scale up to 90% (from an 80% base) across three challenge types — Nexus (2-Step, $139 for $25K) and Lightning (1-Step, $199 for $25K) among them, both carrying a 3% daily loss limit and scaling toward $1M–$1.5M depending on platform. Trustpilot puts ThinkCapital around 4.2–4.3 out of 5 from 600+ reviews, a solid score, alongside some reported payout disputes. One thing worth flagging: several review sites date the ThinkCapital challenge program's launch to 2024, notably more recent than the four years currently tracked here — the gap may reflect ThinkMarkets' longer operating history as the backing broker, but it's worth confirming which figure the four years is meant to describe. Rules and pricing above are third-party sourced and not yet independently verified.

name: Tradeify
desc: $250M+ in verified payouts, 0% payout denial rate claimed, and EOD-trailing drawdown across Growth, Select and Lightning (instant) plans.
tags: No activation fee on any plan
EOD trailing drawdown — no intraday traps
Time-limited code AUG: 40% off (5 uses), then 30% off, ends 31 Aug 2026
review: Tradeify has grown quickly since its 2024 launch by leaning hard into two things: payout speed and rule simplicity. All three account tracks - Growth (pass in 1 day), Select (pass in 3 days, daily payouts once funded) and Lightning (instant funding, no evaluation) - use an end-of-day trailing drawdown rather than an intraday one, which the firm markets as eliminating "intraday traps." Pricing is a one-time payment with no activation fee: a $25K Growth evaluation lists at $99, Select at $109, and a $25K Lightning (instant) account at $345, though a limited-time code (AUG, 40% off first 5 uses then 30% off, expiring 31 Aug 2026) cuts those meaningfully at checkout. Growth carries no consistency rule but a modest daily loss limit; Select drops the daily loss limit but adds a 40% consistency requirement; Lightning funded accounts carry a 20% consistency rule and a capped first-payout amount. The flat 90/10 split applies across all three. Tradeify reports over $250 million in verified payouts and a 0% payout-denial rate, with a 4.8 Trustpilot rating - strong numbers for a firm this young, though the multiple account types and reset-fee structure are worth reading closely before choosing a track.

name: Take Profit Trader
desc: Known for same-day payout access on PRO accounts and a straightforward one-step test.
review: Take Profit Trader runs a simple one-step Test before funding, then splits its funded tier into PRO (80% split) and PRO+ (90/10), with PRO account holders able to request withdrawals from the day they go live rather than waiting for a set cycle - same-day payout access is the firm's headline differentiator. The $25K Test runs around $150/month, targeting $1,500 profit with an EOD trailing drawdown and a $500 daily loss limit; larger accounts scale proportionally up to $150K. Founded in 2021 by James Sixsmith in Orlando, Florida, Take Profit Trader has built a strong track record relatively quickly - a 4.4-star Trustpilot rating from over 9,000 reviews, rated 'Excellent,' with traders regularly praising the payout process and customer service. For traders who value being able to pull profits immediately rather than on a fixed cycle, the PRO account's same-day access is a genuine edge over subscription-based competitors that gate withdrawals to specific windows.

name: Elite Trader Funding
desc: Budget futures evaluations with frequent sales and multiple drawdown styles.
review: Elite Trader Funding's pitch is straightforward: cheap futures evaluations that get cheaper. The tracked $100K 1-Step eval runs $75/mo before discounts, and frequent sales push that lower still — among the least expensive $100K futures challenges we track. The split structure is unusual and trader-friendly on paper: you keep 100% of the first $12.5K in profits before the split drops to 90/10. Multiple drawdown styles (static and trailing options) add flexibility other budget futures firms skip. Trustpilot backs this up at scale — 3.8/5 from over 1,000 reviews, rated "Great" — with traders reporting payouts inside 48 hours and one first payout confirmed within six trading sessions. But nearly a quarter of reviews are one-star, clustered around payout declines and rule disputes after traders hit meaningful profit. Elite Trader Funding isn't broker-backed, so read recent reviews before funding a larger account, and keep records of every trade in case a payout is contested.

trustNote: Reported as 4.6–4.7/5 across thousands of reviews.
name: Earn2Trade
desc: Education-first futures firm; Gauntlet Mini evaluation feeds funded accounts at partner firms.
review: Earn2Trade differentiates itself by leading with education rather than a bare evaluation. The Gauntlet Mini — the plan we track, ~$170/mo for a $50K account — bundles structured coursework with the challenge itself, and passing traders move onto the Trader Career Path for further scaling at partner funders. The 80/20 split is below the futures-firm norm (most competitors offer 90/10), the trade-off for the education layer and career-path structure. Founded in 2016, Earn2Trade is one of the longer-tenured names in futures prop trading, and it shows in the Trustpilot record: 4.6–4.7/5 "Excellent" from thousands of reviews, among the strongest ratings of any firm in this dataset. The catch is that Earn2Trade funds traders via partner firms rather than its own balance sheet, so payout terms and account details ultimately depend on which partner you land with — worth confirming before you commit to the $170/mo subscription.

trustNote: Reported as 4.7–4.8/5.
name: Bulenox
desc: Deep-discount futures evaluations — promo pricing regularly cuts list prices by 80–90%.
review: Bulenox's list prices are close to meaningless — the firm runs near-constant promo pricing that cuts 80–90% off, and the $16 entry we track for a $10K futures evaluation reflects that reality rather than an outlier. Founded in 2022 and based in Wilmington, Delaware, Bulenox has built a strong reputation fast: 4.7–4.8/5 "Excellent" on Trustpilot from close to 1,000 reviews, with traders consistently citing transparent rules and reliable payouts. The 90/10 split matches the futures-firm standard, and a choice between trailing and EOD drawdown gives some flexibility on risk style. The main thing to watch is that this is a young firm still building its long-term track record, and — as with any deep-discount model — it's worth checking that the promo price you're quoted matches what's live on their site before you buy, since list-price comparisons across firms won't reflect what anyone actually pays here.

trustNote: Bimodal distribution — 68% five-star, 25% one-star — rather than a smooth average.
name: Phidias
desc: Lowest static-drawdown entry point in futures at $55 for a $25K account.
review: Phidias carved out a specific niche: the lowest static-drawdown entry point we track in futures, $55 for a $25K account with no daily loss limit. Founded in 2023 by two French traders and based in Gibraltar, it's a newer name — the firm reports over 10,000 registered traders as of early 2026, and offers four account types (Static, Fundamental, Swing, and the larger Master Account) up to $1M in funding, with a 90/10 split on the plan we track. Trustpilot paints a polarized picture: 3.9/5 from 273 reviews, but the breakdown is bimodal — 68% five-star against 25% one-star, not a smooth middle-of-the-road score. Positive reviews cite reliable payouts and responsive support; negative ones center on platform stability and how outages, including Rithmic feed issues, were handled. Given the short operating history and the split rating, this is one to size cautiously into rather than fund a large account with on day one.

trustNote: Reported in the 4.3–4.5 range across several thousand reviews.
name: FXIFY
desc: 1, 2 & 3-Phase plus Instant models with account sizes up to $400K. EAs, weekend holds and news trading allowed on most plans.
review: FXIFY's core appeal is flexibility: 1, 2 and 3-Phase evaluations plus an Instant option, scaling to $400K accounts, with EAs, weekend holding and news trading allowed on most plans - a looser rule set than most forex competitors, who typically restrict at least one of those. The catch is that HFT and latency arbitrage are explicitly banned, so the leniency has limits. Base split is 75-90%, with a paid add-on pushing it to 90% on the base 1-Step. List pricing looks mid-pack ($199 for a $25K 1-Step, ~$550 for $100K) but 30-60% discount codes are close to constant, so few traders pay sticker price. Payouts run on a two-week cycle with roughly 24-hour processing once approved. On Trustpilot, FXIFY sits in the 4.3-4.5 range across several thousand reviews, with the five-star count growing faster than the one-star count even as both rise - a reasonably healthy trend for a firm scaling this fast.

trustNote: Trustpilot data is inconsistent across sources — ratings reported anywhere from 3.1 to 4.5–4.6 depending on source and date.
name: Instant Funding
desc: No-challenge instant-funded accounts alongside a traditional evaluation option — capital access from day one.
tags: Trade with real capital on day one
review: Instant Funding's pitch is straightforward: trade with real capital from day one via its no-challenge Instant accounts, or take the cheaper traditional Evaluation route if you'd rather prove yourself first - a $50K 2-Step evaluation runs around $89, while a $10K Instant account lists near $199. The catch on the Instant side is a tighter, intraday-trailing 10% drawdown with a 4% daily loss cap and no weekend holding, notably stricter than the firm's own evaluated accounts. List prices are close to meaningless in practice, since 30-60% discount codes run almost constantly. Trustpilot data on this firm is genuinely inconsistent across sources - ratings ranging from as low as 3.1 to as high as 4.5-4.6 depending on when and where you look - and a meaningful share of negative reviews describe payout requests denied over alleged rule violations, including at least one reported case involving a withheld payout above $21,000. That spread is wide enough that we'd treat any single aggregate score with caution and recommend reading recent, dated reviews before funding beyond the cheapest tier.

name: Funded Trading Plus
desc: Founded 2013 as Trade Room Plus. Simplified 2026 lineup: Instant, 1-Step Express and 2-Step Classic.
tags: No consistency rule, no min trading days
Instant option carries a pricing premium
review: Funded Trading Plus traces back to 2013 as Trade Room Plus, giving it a longer operating history than most prop firms competing today, and its 2026 lineup has been simplified to three tracks: Instant, 1-Step Express and 2-Step Classic. The 1-Step Express starts at $119 for a $25K account - 80-100% split, 6% trailing drawdown, 4% daily loss - with no consistency rule and no minimum trading days on either evaluation path, a real convenience for traders who don't want their schedule dictated by the firm. Splits climb from 80% toward 100% at profit milestones (roughly 30% cumulative), among the higher ceilings in the forex category. Payouts run weekly, arriving in 1-3 days; the Instant option carries a pricing premium over the evaluated tracks. Funded Trading Plus reports paying out more than $19.5 million to over 60,000 traders across 180+ countries, and holds a 4.7-star Trustpilot rating from more than 2,400 reviews - 92% of them five-star, one of the stronger reputations in this comparison.

trustNote: Reported in the 4.0–4.4 range from several hundred reviews.
name: Lux Trading Firm
desc: London-based, founded 2020. Real A-book execution with scaling up to $10M across multiple stages.
tags: Withdrawn profits still count toward targets
0% daily loss allowance on funded accounts
review: Lux Trading Firm's defining feature is its execution model: unlike the vast majority of prop firms running simulated accounts, Lux operates on a genuine A-Book basis, routing funded trades directly to liquidity providers with no dealing desk - and its payout track record has been KPMG-audited, a rare third-party verification in an industry that mostly asks you to take its word for it. The single 2-Step Evaluation scales all the way to $10M across multiple funding stages, among the highest ceilings tracked here, and withdrawn profits still count toward your scaling targets rather than resetting progress. The trade-offs are real: a mandatory stop-loss on every trade and a 0% daily loss allowance on funded accounts, both stricter than typical forex challenge terms. A $100K evaluation runs around £199 (~$269). London-based and launched in 2020-2021 (sources vary on the exact date) under founder Petra Pirova, Lux carries a Trustpilot rating in the 4.0-4.4 range from several hundred reviews - solid, though a smaller sample than the largest retail-focused firms.

trustNote: No independent Trustpilot score cited. Separately, the firm is mid-way through a trust event (Premium plan discontinued Jul 2026 amid pending-payout disputes) — see firm tags.
name: Alpha Futures
desc: UK-based futures-only sister brand of Alpha Capital Group, founded 2024. EOD trailing drawdown with 90% split from day one on Advanced accounts. Premium plan discontinued Jul 2026 (see trust warning tag); Zero and Advanced plans continue, migrating to the in-house AlphaTrader platform.
tags: Zero option has no activation fee
TRUST WARNING: Premium plan closed Jul 12 2026, pending payouts converted to refunds; lost NinjaTrader/Tradovate, migrating to in-house platform
review: Alpha Futures is in the middle of a genuine trust event, and traders considering it should know the details before signing up. On July 12, 2026, the firm discontinued its Premium plan entirely - stating it had paid out more than $25 million on that plan in two months at a loss - and simultaneously lost its NinjaTrader and Tradovate integrations after the platforms ended their partnership. Traders on the Premium plan had their accounts closed and fees refunded, but multiple independent reports indicate pending payouts earned under that plan were not honored, which is the more serious concern. The Zero and Advanced plans continue on paper, still offering a 90% split from day one (Advanced) and weekly payouts up to $15,000 per request, but every trader is now migrating to Alpha's in-house AlphaTrader platform rather than the third-party rails they originally signed up for. Until Alpha demonstrates it is honoring outstanding payout obligations and the new platform proves reliable, we'd treat this as a firm to watch from the sidelines rather than fund through right now.

name: Smart Prop Trader
desc: 2-Step evaluation with no minimum trading days and split scaling from 75% up to 95% based on performance milestones.
review: Smart Prop Trader runs a single, low-friction format: a 2-Step evaluation with no minimum trading days, an 8% static drawdown, and a 4% daily loss limit, priced from $57 for a $5K account up to roughly $497 for $100K. Its split structure is the standout — starting at 75% and climbing in 5% increments to a 95% ceiling as milestones are hit, with an automatic bump to 90/10 if the account grows 25% in a quarter. The firm runs on DXtrade rather than the more common MT5/cTrader pairing, and its own tag data flags the underlying broker/platform as unregulated — worth weighing against the firm's 4.5/5 Trustpilot rating from over 2,500 reviews. Founded in mid-2022, matching the four years tracked here. Reviews skew mixed-to-positive on price and instant-funding mechanics but light on volume. Treat this as a budget option worth sizing cautiously into rather than a firm with a fully verified track record.

review: BluSky Trading Company is a Florida-based futures firm operating since 2022 with a broad account menu: Launch (a 4-phase evaluation aimed at the lowest entry cost), Propel Premium and Propel Static (EOD-trailing vs. fixed drawdown), Orbit (funded in as little as a day, no evaluation-phase consistency rule), Instant Sim (no evaluation at all), and Direct 2 Funded (split scaling 50%→80%). The firm's headline features are daily Monday-through-Friday payouts with no minimum trading-day requirement on several plans, splits up to 90%, and support for seven platforms including NinjaTrader, Tradovate and Rithmic. The main rule to plan around is a 30% consistency requirement — no single trading day can account for more than 30% of your profit target — which applies across most plans. BluSky reports over $10 million paid out since launch and carries a strong Trustpilot reputation (5.0/5 from 800+ reviews). Rule specifics like exact drawdown percentages vary meaningfully by plan and aren't fully confirmed here — verify the current terms on blusky.pro before funding.

review: OneUp Trader has been running since 2016 out of Wilmington, Delaware, making it one of the more tenured futures firms in this list. Evaluations are single-phase with no time limit — hit a 6% profit target within a 3.5% trailing drawdown and a limited contract count, with a light consistency rule (three other days summing to at least 80% of your best day) that only applies during the evaluation. Pricing runs $65 for a $25K account up to $325 for $250K, and unusually, you only pay half the fee upfront with the rest due once you pass. Funded traders keep 100% of their first $10,000 in withdrawals before moving to a 90/10 split. Trustpilot backs the reputation with a 4.7/5 from over 2,400 reviews — one of the stronger review bases among futures-only firms.
